bituriges-vivisci.e: Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:bordeaux|Burdigala]] became the capital of [[e:gallia-aquitania|Aquitania]] and a rich city whose vineyards, based on a vine named Biturica after the people, laid the foundations of the Bordeaux wine trade. The poet [[e:ausonius|Ausonius]] was born there in the 4th century.

boii-400.t: Celtic people who settled the plain around Bologna around 400 BCE and fought Rome for two centuries before being defeated in 191 BCE.
boii-400.o: The [[s:boii|Boii]] crossed the [[e:alps|Alps]] into the Po valley around 400 BCE, part of the great Celtic migration into [[e:italy|Italy]]. They settled the plain south of the Po in modern [[e:emilia|Emilia]], taking over the Etruscan city of [[s:felsina|Felsina]], which became [[e:bologna|Bononia]]. Other Boii lived north of the Alps in [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], which bears their name.
boii-400.r: The [[e:cisalpine-gaul|Cisalpine]] [[s:boii|Boii]] were organised in many clans under chiefs, living in villages and small towns and farming the rich plain; they raised pigs and grain. [[e:polybius|Polybius]] describes their warrior elites, whose wealth lay in [[e:cattle|cattle]] and gold. Together with the [[s:insubres|Insubres]] they were the main Gaulish power in [[e:italy|Italy]], fighting [[e:rome|Rome]] at [[e:battle-of-telamon|Telamon]] in 225 BCE.
boii-400.e: In 218 BCE they attacked [[e:rome|Rome's]] new colonies at [[s:plaisance|Placentia]] and [[s:commune-of-cremona|Cremona]] and supported [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]]; in 216 BCE they ambushed and killed the consul-elect [[e:lucius-postumius-albinus-consul-234-bc|Postumius]]. [[e:publius-cornelius-scipio-nasica-consul-191-bc|Publius Cornelius Scipio Nasica]] defeated them in 191 BCE and confiscated half their land, and Rome founded [[e:bologna|Bononia]] in 189 BCE.

british-administration-of-eritrea.t: The British military and civil administration of the former Italian colony while the world powers and the UN decided Eritrea's future.
british-administration-of-eritrea.o: After defeating the Italians at [[e:keren|Keren]] and taking [[e:asmara|Asmara]] in 1941, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] administered [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] as occupied enemy territory under the laws of war. The peace treaty of 1947 required [[e:italy|Italy]] to give up its colonies, but the four powers could not agree on [[e:eritrea|Eritrea's]] fate and referred it to the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]].
british-administration-of-eritrea.r: The British kept much of the Italian administration and allowed political parties, trade unions and newspapers in [[e:tigrinya-language|Tigrinya]] and Arabic. Rival parties formed: the Unionists favoured union with [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]], the [[e:muslim-league-of-eritrea|Muslim League]] and others independence. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] dismantled and sold some industrial plant. A UN commission visited in 1950, and political violence by shifta bands disturbed the countryside.
british-administration-of-eritrea.e: In December 1950 the [[e:united-nations-general-assembly|UN General Assembly]] decided that [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] should be federated with [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]]. British administration ended in September 1952, when the [[e:eritrea|Eritrea]] federation came into being.

boii-of-gaul.t: Band of Boii who joined the Helvetian migration of 58 BCE and were resettled by Caesar in Aeduan territory.
boii-of-gaul.o: The [[s:boii|Boii]] were a widespread Celtic people known in [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], which takes its name from them, and in northern [[e:italy|Italy]]. Caesar records that thirty-two thousand Boii joined the [[s:helvetii|Helvetii]] in 58 BCE after besieging [[e:noreia|Noreia]] in [[s:kingdom-of-noricum|Noricum]].
boii-of-gaul.r: After the defeat of the [[s:helvetii|Helvetii]] near [[e:bibracte|Bibracte]], the [[s:aedui|Aedui]] asked Caesar to let the [[s:boii|Boii]] settle in their land because of their courage. They received the town of [[e:gorgobina|Gorgobina]], perhaps near Saint-Parize-le-Châtel.
boii-of-gaul.e: In 52 BCE [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]] besieged [[e:gorgobina|Gorgobina]] to punish them for their loyalty to [[e:rome|Rome]], and Caesar marched to their relief. They later vanish as a separate group within the Aeduan civitas.

boina.t: The northern Sakalava kingdom of Madagascar, whose port of Mahajanga became a thriving hub of Indian Ocean trade in the 18th century.
boina.o: Boina was founded around 1690 by [[e:andriamandisoarivo|Andriamandisoarivo]], a prince of the [[e:maroserana-dynasty|Maroserana dynasty]] of [[s:menabe|Menabe]], who led followers north and conquered the north-west coast. The kingdom took over the trading towns of the [[e:antalaotra|Antalaotra]], Swahili-speaking Muslim merchants, and later centred on [[e:mahajanga|Majunga]] (Mahajanga).
boina.r: [[e:sakalava|Sakalava]] kingship rested on sacred royal relics and ancestor cults, while Muslim and Indian merchants ran the port trade in slaves, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and [[e:rice|rice]] with [[e:arabia|Arabia]], the [[e:swahili|Swahili]] coast and the [[e:comoro-islands|Comoros]]. Boina reached its height under Queen [[e:ravahiny|Ravahiny]] in the late 18th century, when [[e:mahajanga|Mahajanga]] was one of the busiest ports in the western [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]].
boina.e: The [[s:merina-kingdom|Merina Kingdom]] under [[e:radama-i|Radama I]] captured [[e:mahajanga|Mahajanga]] in 1824. King [[e:andriantsoly|Andriantsoly]] fled and later took over the [[s:sultanate-of-mayotte|Sultanate of Mayotte]], and [[e:sakalava|Sakalava]] resistance in Boina collapsed by around 1840. Royal relic rituals still take place at Mahajanga.
boina.re: Traditional Malagasy religion, Islam among merchants

british-windward-islands.t: Grouping of Britain's southern Caribbean islands under one governor from 1833 to 1960, linking Grenada, Saint Vincent, Saint Lucia and later Dominica.
british-windward-islands.o: In 1833 the British government placed [[s:barbados|Barbados]], [[s:grenada|Grenada]], [[e:saint-vincent-island|Saint Vincent]] and [[e:tobago|Tobago]] under a single governor-in-chief resident in [[e:bridgetown|Bridgetown]], to cut costs and coordinate the transition from [[e:slavery|slavery]]. [[s:saint-lucia|Saint Lucia]] was added in 1838.
british-windward-islands.r: The [[e:windward-islands|Windward Islands]] was an administrative union rather than a federation: each island kept its own laws, treasury and, at first, assembly, under a lieutenant governor or administrator. Most islands became crown colonies in the 1870s. [[s:barbados|Barbados]] resisted plans for closer union, and riots in 1876 led to its withdrawal in 1885, after which the governor resided at [[e:st-georges-grenada|St George's]], [[s:grenada|Grenada]]. [[e:tobago|Tobago]] left for [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] in 1889, and [[s:commonwealth-of-dominica|Dominica]] joined from the [[e:leeward-islands|Leeward Islands]] in 1940.
british-windward-islands.e: The member islands entered the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]] in 1958, and the [[e:windward-islands|Windward Islands]] governorship was abolished in 1960. Its members later became independent as [[s:grenada|Grenada]], [[s:saint-vincent-and-the-grenadines|Saint Vincent and the Grenadines]], [[s:saint-lucia|Saint Lucia]] and [[s:commonwealth-of-dominica|Dominica]].

bit-zamani.t: Bit Zamani, an Aramaean kingdom on the upper Tigris around Amedi, modern Diyarbakır, absorbed by Assyria in the 9th century BCE.
bit-zamani.o: Aramaean groups established Bit Zamani on the upper [[e:tigris|Tigris]] after the [[e:late-bronze-age-collapse|Late Bronze Age collapse]], with its capital at [[e:amadiya|Amedi]], the city that became [[e:diyarbakir|Diyarbakır]]. It appears in Assyrian sources from the late 10th century BCE.
bit-zamani.r: Its rulers controlled the routes between [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] and the [[e:copper|copper]] of [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. Ammi-ba'al made a treaty with [[e:ashurnasirpal-ii|Ashurnasirpal II]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] but was murdered by rebels in 879 BCE, prompting an Assyrian campaign.
bit-zamani.e: Assyrian kings reduced Bit Zamani to a [[e:vassal|vassal]] and then, by the late 9th century BCE, a province called [[e:amadiya|Amedi]]. The city has remained a regional centre ever since.

burgraviate-of-friedberg.t: Unusual corporate state of the castle knights of Friedberg, who elected their burgrave and became the leading power of the Wetterau.
burgraviate-of-friedberg.o: The [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] built [[e:friedberg-hesse|Friedberg]] castle in the [[e:wetterau|Wetterau]] in the 12th century and garrisoned it with castle men, imperial knights who lived in the fortress. The burgrave, their commander, is documented from 1216. Over time the knights formed a self-governing corporation that elected the burgrave from their own ranks.
burgraviate-of-friedberg.r: The Burgraviate was governed by the burgrave and an assembly of castle knights, a kind of aristocratic republic. It acquired the Free Court of Kaichen and gradually took control over the neighbouring [[s:free-imperial-city-of-friedberg|Free Imperial City of Friedberg]], which shared the hill. Its knights also led the [[e:wetterau|Wetterau]] imperial knights. Most members accepted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in the 16th century.
burgraviate-of-friedberg.e: The Burgraviate survived until the end of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]], when it was mediatised and absorbed into the [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Grand Duchy of Hesse]] in 1806. The castle still dominates [[e:friedberg-hesse|Friedberg]] in [[e:hesse|Hesse]].

british-guiana.t: Britain's colony on the South American mainland, a sugar colony whose Indian, African, Portuguese and Chinese communities shaped modern Guyana.
british-guiana.o: In 1831 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] united the colonies of [[s:demerara-essequibo|Demerara-Essequibo]] and [[s:berbice|Berbice]] into British Guiana, with [[e:georgetown-guyana|Georgetown]] as capital. [[e:slavery|Slavery]] was abolished in 1834, and after the apprenticeship period ended in 1838 most freed people left the plantations to found their own villages.
british-guiana.r: Planters replaced them with indentured labourers, mostly from [[e:india|India]] from 1838, as well as Portuguese from [[e:madeira|Madeira]] and Chinese workers. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] remained dominant, with bauxite mining growing in the 20th century. An international tribunal in 1899 settled the western border with [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]]. In 1953 the [[e:peoples-progressive-party-guyana|People's Progressive Party]] of [[e:cheddi-jagan|Cheddi Jagan]] won elections, but [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] suspended the constitution after 133 days. Politics then split between Jagan and [[e:forbes-burnham|Forbes Burnham]].
british-guiana.e: Racial violence between Indian and African Guyanese followed in the early 1960s. British Guiana gained independence on 26 May 1966 as [[s:co-operative-republic-of-guyana|Guyana]], later the Co-operative Republic of Guyana, with [[e:forbes-burnham|Burnham]] as prime minister.

bima-sultanate.t: Muslim sultanate of eastern Sumbawa, a close ally of Makassar whose court chronicles and palace survived into the Indonesian republic.
bima-sultanate.o: Bima, the land of the [[e:bima-people|Mbojo]] people, had been a [[e:hindu-buddhist|Hindu-Buddhist]] kingdom tied to [[e:java|Java]] before its rulers accepted [[e:islam|Islam]] under the influence of the [[e:sultanate-of-gowa|Gowa Sultanate of Makassar]]. Its first sultan, [[e:abdul-kahir|Abdul Kahir]], took power around 1620 to 1640, and intermarriage with the Makassarese royal house bound the two courts closely together.
bima-sultanate.r: The sultan ruled with a council of nobles and a hereditary chief minister, the Tureli Nggampo, while Islamic scholars advised on law. Bima exported horses, [[e:rice|rice]], sappanwood and textiles, and its court kept a chronicle, the [[e:bo-sangaji-kai|Bo Sangaji Kai]]. After the fall of [[s:gowa-sultanate|Makassar]] it signed a treaty with the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] in 1669.
bima-sultanate.e: The 1815 eruption of [[e:mount-tambora|Mount Tambora]] devastated the land and destroyed the neighbouring [[s:kingdom-of-tambora|Kingdom of Tambora]]. Bima remained a self-governing domain of the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]], and its last sultan, [[e:muhammad-salahuddin-of-bima|Muhammad Salahuddin]], brought it into [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]]. Its special status ended in 1958; the palace is now a museum.

bangladesh.t: The densely populated Bengali nation of the Ganges delta, born in 1971 from a war of liberation against Pakistan.
bangladesh.o: [[e:east-bengal|East Bengal]] became part of the [[s:dominion-of-pakistan|Dominion of Pakistan]] in 1947 and was renamed [[e:east-pakistan|East Pakistan]] in 1955. Grievances over language, economics and political power grew, and when the [[e:awami-league|Awami League]] under [[e:sheikh-mujibur-rahman|Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]] won the 1970 election but was denied office, the Pakistani army cracked down in March 1971. Independence was declared and, after a war with Indian support, secured in December 1971.
bangladesh.r: [[e:sheikh-mujibur-rahman|Sheikh Mujib]] led the new state until his assassination in 1975; military rulers [[e:ziaur-rahman|Ziaur Rahman]] and [[e:hussain-muhammad-ershad|Hussain Muhammad Ershad]] followed. Parliamentary democracy returned in 1991, dominated by [[e:khaleda-zia|Khaleda Zia]] and [[e:sheikh-hasina|Sheikh Hasina]]. Bangladesh has grown through garment exports, remittances and microfinance, pioneered by the [[e:grameen-bank|Grameen Bank]], while facing cyclones and floods.
bangladesh.e: The republic continues; mass protests in 2024 forced [[e:sheikh-hasina|Sheikh Hasina]] from office, and an interim government under [[e:muhammad-yunus|Muhammad Yunus]] took charge and organised elections in February 2026. Bangladesh remains one of the most densely populated countries and a leading garment exporter.

cr.a: See File history below for details.

banpur-state.t: A Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand whose Raja joined the revolt of 1857, leading to its confiscation by the British.
banpur-state.o: Banpur was a [[e:bundelas|Bundela]] principality in the hills south of [[s:jhansi-state|Jhansi]], held by a branch of the [[e:bundela|Bundela]] clan. The register dates it from around 1650, though its early history is not well documented.
banpur-state.r: Its Rajas ruled a small upland territory with forts and agricultural villages. In the 1850s Raja Mardan Singh of Banpur joined the uprising of 1857 against the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]], fighting alongside other [[e:bundelas|Bundela]] chiefs.
banpur-state.e: After the revolt was suppressed in 1858, the British confiscated Banpur and added it to their own territory. Its lands now lie in [[e:lalitpur-district|Lalitpur district]] of [[e:uttar-pradesh|Uttar Pradesh]].

batlhaping-chiefdom.t: The southernmost Tswana chiefdom, whose capital Dithakong received the first European missions in the Tswana world.
batlhaping-chiefdom.o: The Batlhaping branched from the [[e:barolong|Barolong]] and by the 18th century were settled along the margins of the southern Kalahari around Dithakong and the Kuruman river. Their large town impressed Cape officials who visited in 1801, reporting a population of many thousands.
batlhaping-chiefdom.r: Chiefs such as Molehabangwe and his son Mothibi ruled through wards and the kgotla, with an economy of [[e:cattle|cattle]], hunting and trade in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and skins with the Cape. The [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] settled among them, and [[e:robert-moffat|Robert Moffat]] established the Kuruman mission in the 1820s. In 1823 Tlhaping and [[e:griqua|Griqua]] forces repelled a large army of displaced invaders at the [[e:battle-of-dithakong|Battle of Dithakong]].
batlhaping-chiefdom.e: Diamond discoveries, [[e:griqua|Griqua]] and [[e:boers|Boer]] land claims and the annexation of [[s:griqualand-west|Griqualand West]] reduced Tlhaping lands. In 1885 they became part of [[s:british-bechuanaland|British Bechuanaland]], and a rising under [[e:galeshewe|Galeshewe]] in 1896–97 was crushed.

baiocasses.t: Gallic people of the Bessin in Normandy whose town Augustodurum grew into Bayeux.
baiocasses.o: Known from [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny]] and later Roman sources, the Baiocasses lived along the [[e:calvados|Calvados]] coast west of the [[e:orne-river|Orne]]. In Caesar's day they were probably counted among the Armorican peoples.
baiocasses.r: No rulers or pre-Roman institutions are recorded.
baiocasses.e: Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town was [[e:bayeux|Augustodurum]], renamed Baiocasses in late antiquity, the origin of Bayeux. It became a bishopric, and in the 11th century the [[e:bayeux-tapestry|Bayeux Tapestry]] was made for its cathedral.

bahmani-sultanate.t: The first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan, whose rulers built Gulbarga and Bidar and fought a long rivalry with Vijayanagara.
bahmani-sultanate.o: In 1347 rebel nobles of the [[e:deccan|Deccan]] revolted against [[e:muhammad-bin-tughluq|Muhammad bin Tughluq]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]]. Their leader, [[e:ala-ud-din-bahman-shah|Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah]], was proclaimed sultan at [[e:daulatabad|Daulatabad]] and made [[e:kalaburagi|Gulbarga]] his capital, founding a dynasty that controlled the Deccan from the [[e:arabian-sea|Arabian Sea]] towards the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]].
bahmani-sultanate.r: The sultanate was divided into four, later eight, provinces governed by tarafdars. Its court attracted Persian, Turkic and Arab immigrants, whose rivalry with local Deccani Muslims shaped politics. [[e:ahmad-shah-i-wali|Ahmad Shah I]] moved the capital to [[e:bidar|Bidar]]. The minister [[e:mahmud-gawan|Mahmud Gawan]] reformed administration and built a great [[e:madrasa|madrasa]] at Bidar. Wars with the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] over the [[e:raichur-doab|Raichur Doab]] recurred for 150 years.
bahmani-sultanate.e: After [[e:mahmud-gawan|Mahmud Gawan's]] execution in 1481 the provincial governors became independent, creating the [[s:bijapur-sultanate|Bijapur Sultanate]], [[s:ahmadnagar-sultanate|Ahmadnagar Sultanate]], [[s:berar-sultanate|Berar Sultanate]], [[s:golconda-sultanate|Golconda Sultanate]] and [[s:bidar-sultanate|Bidar Sultanate]]. The last Bahmani sultans were puppets of the Barid Shahis until about 1527.

bergistani.t: A small Iberian people of the Catalan pre-Pyrenees whose repeated revolts against Cato in 195 BCE ended in their enslavement.
bergistani.o: The Bergistani lived in the upper [[e:llobregat|Llobregat]] valley of central [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]], a region still called the [[e:bergueda|Berguedà]] after them. They were an Iberian-speaking hill people whose main stronghold was the fortress of [[e:bergium|Bergium]], perhaps near modern [[e:berga|Berga]].
bergistani.r: Little is known about their society beyond [[e:livy|Livy's]] narrative. They lived from mixed farming and herding in a mountainous district and defended themselves from fortified hilltops.
bergistani.e: In 195 BCE they rose twice against the consul [[e:cato-the-elder|Cato]]. After the second revolt he took their strongholds and sold the inhabitants into [[e:slavery|slavery]], and [[e:bergium|Bergium]] itself fell when its chief, who said brigands had seized it, helped the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] inside. The territory was absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]].

beylik-of-tunis.t: Tunisia under the Husainid beys, autonomous within the Ottoman world, which issued the Arab world's first constitution before falling under French rule.
beylik-of-tunis.o: In 1705, during an invasion from the [[s:regency-of-algiers|Regency of Algiers]], the cavalry officer [[e:husayn-ibn-ali|Husayn ibn Ali]] seized power in [[e:tunis|Tunis]] and founded the [[e:husainid-dynasty|Husainid dynasty]]. Succeeding [[s:ottoman-tunisia|Ottoman Tunisia]], the beys acknowledged Ottoman [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] but ruled as hereditary princes.
beylik-of-tunis.r: [[e:hammuda-ibn-ali|Hammuda Pasha]], ruling from 1782 to 1814, brought prosperity and independence from [[e:algiers|Algiers]]. [[e:ahmad-i-bey|Ahmad Bey]] modernised the army and abolished [[e:slavery|slavery]] in 1846. A [[e:fundamental-pact|Fundamental Pact]] of 1857 and the constitution of 1861 limited the bey's power, and [[e:khayr-al-din-al-tunisi|Khayr al-Din]] pursued reforms. But heavy debts led to an international financial commission in 1869.
beylik-of-tunis.e: [[e:france|France]] invaded in 1881, and the [[e:treaty-of-bardo|Treaty of Bardo]] created the [[s:french-protectorate-of-tunisia|French protectorate of Tunisia]]. The beys reigned under French control until independence in 1956, when [[e:muhammad-al-amin-bey|Muhammad al-Amin Bey]] became king of the [[s:kingdom-of-tunisia|Kingdom of Tunisia]].

bansda-state.t: A Solanki Rajput state in the forested hills of southern Gujarat, beside the Dangs.
bansda-state.o: The rulers of Vansda (Bansda) were Solanki [[e:rajputs|Rajputs]] whose line claimed descent from the [[e:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukya]] kings of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. Their small hill state emerged as a distinct principality in the 18th century and came under [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] and then British supervision.
bansda-state.r: Bansda was a 9-gun salute state of the [[e:surat-agency|Surat Agency]], later the [[e:gujarat-states-agency|Gujarat States Agency]], governed by a Maharawal over a forested, largely Adivasi territory of [[e:kokna-people|Kokna]], [[e:bhils|Bhil]] and other communities. [[e:timber|Timber]] and forest produce were the main resources.
bansda-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Bansda was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. Its former forests are protected in the [[e:vansda-national-park|Vansda National Park]] in Navsari district.

breuci.t: Pannonian people of the lower Sava valley who led, and then betrayed, the great revolt against Rome of 6–9 CE.
breuci.o: The Breuci lived along the lower [[e:sava|Sava]] in modern [[e:croatia|Croatia]], [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]] and [[s:serbia|Serbia]], among the Pannonian peoples of the region. They appear in Roman sources as Roman armies pushed into the Sava valley.
breuci.r: Known mainly from Roman accounts, they were a populous tribal people of farmers and stockbreeders, said to field large armies. In 6 CE, when [[e:rome|Rome]] levied troops for a war against the [[s:marcomanni|Marcomanni]], they rose under [[e:bato-the-breucian|Bato the Breucian]] and [[e:pinnes|Pinnes]], joining the [[e:daesitiates|Daesitiates]] in the [[e:great-illyrian-revolt|Great Illyrian Revolt]].
breuci.e: In 8 CE [[e:bato-the-breucian|Bato the Breucian]] surrendered [[e:pinnes|Pinnes]] to [[e:rome|Rome]] and was then executed by [[e:bato-the-daesitiate|Bato of the Daesitiates]]. The Breuci submitted, and their young men were enrolled in Roman auxiliary units, the [[e:cohort|cohortes]] Breucorum, that served across the empire.

baekje.t: A southwestern Korean kingdom of the Three Kingdoms period, celebrated for refined Buddhist art and for passing writing and Buddhism to Japan.
baekje.o: Tradition holds that [[e:onjo-of-baekje|Onjo]], a son of Goguryeo's founder, established Baekje in 18 BCE at [[e:wiryeseong|Wiryeseong]] on the Han river. It began as one statelet of the [[s:mahan|Mahan confederacy]] and grew to dominate it, reaching its peak under [[e:geunchogo-of-baekje|King Geunchogo]], who killed a [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] king in battle in 371.
baekje.r: An aristocracy of leading clans served kings who traced descent from [[s:buyeo|Buyeo]]. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] arrived in 384. Driven south by [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] in 475, the court moved to [[e:gongju|Ungjin]] (Gongju) and in 538 to Sabi. Baekje traded with southern Chinese dynasties and maintained close ties to [[s:yamato|Yamato]], sending scholars, artisans and Buddhist images; the gilt-bronze [[e:incense|incense]] burner and King [[e:muryeong-of-baekje|Muryeong]]'s tomb show its craftsmanship.
baekje.e: King [[e:seong-of-baekje|Seong]] was killed fighting [[s:silla|Silla]] in 554. In 660 a Silla and [[s:later-tang|Tang]] alliance took Sabi and King [[e:uija-of-baekje|Uija]] surrendered. A restoration movement backed by [[s:yamato|Yamato]] was crushed at [[e:battle-of-baekgang|Baekgang]] in 663, and many refugees settled in [[e:japan|Japan]].

bahia-republic.t: The Sabinada, a revolt that proclaimed a republic in Salvador in 1837 until the young Emperor Pedro II came of age, crushed within four months.
bahia-republic.o: During the unstable regency period in the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]], discontent in [[e:salvador|Salvador]] over central control and military recruitment for the war in [[e:rio-grande-do-sul|Rio Grande do Sul]] came to a head. On 7 November 1837 rebels led by the doctor [[e:francisco-sabino-vieira|Francisco Sabino Vieira]] took the city and proclaimed the [[e:bahia|Bahia]] Republic.
bahia-republic.r: The revolt was led by urban professionals, officers and soldiers. Its leaders declared [[e:bahia|Bahia]] independent only until [[e:pedro-ii-of-brazil|Pedro II]] reached adulthood, a compromise reflecting divisions among them. They offered freedom to Brazilian-born enslaved people who fought for the republic. The rebels never controlled the [[e:reconcavo|Recôncavo]] [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] region, whose planters supported the imperial government.
bahia-republic.e: Imperial forces besieged [[e:salvador|Salvador]] by land and sea and retook it in March 1838 after fierce street fighting with heavy loss of life. [[e:francisco-sabino-vieira|Sabino]] was exiled to [[s:captaincy-of-mato-grosso|Mato Grosso]], and the revolt became known as the Sabinada after him.

blue-horde.t: The western wing of the Golden Horde, the realm of Batu and his heirs on the Volga, Don and Dnieper steppes.
blue-horde.o: After the conquest of the western steppe and Rus' between 1236 and 1242, the [[e:jochids|Jochid]] lands were divided into two wings. The western or right wing, ruled by [[e:batu-khan|Batu]] from [[e:sarai|Sarai]] on the lower [[e:volga|Volga]], is often called the Blue Horde, though medieval sources use the colour names inconsistently.
blue-horde.r: The western wing was the core of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]], controlling the Rus' principalities, the [[e:volga|Volga]] trade and the Crimean ports. Its khans, including [[e:berke|Berke]], [[e:uzbek-khan|Uzbek Khan]] and [[e:jani-beg|Jani Beg]], held authority over the whole [[e:jochids|Jochid]] realm. Under its rule [[e:islam|Islam]] spread among the elite and [[e:sarai|Sarai]] grew into a major trading city.
blue-horde.e: After [[e:jani-beg|Jani Beg's]] murder in 1357, decades of civil war followed, and between 1378 and 1380 the [[s:white-horde|White Horde]] khan [[e:tokhtamysh|Tokhtamysh]] seized [[e:sarai|Sarai]] and reunited the two wings. The western lands later broke into the [[s:khanate-of-kazan|Khanate of Kazan]], the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]], the [[s:astrakhan-khanate|Astrakhan Khanate]] and the [[s:great-horde|Great Horde]].

baroda-state.t: The Maratha kingdom of the Gaekwads in Gujarat, one of the richest princely states and, under Sayajirao III, a pioneer of free schooling and public libraries.
baroda-state.o: [[e:pilaji-rao-gaekwad|Pilaji Rao Gaekwad]], a commander serving the Dabhade family and the [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] state, seized [[e:songadh|Songadh]] in 1721 and used it as a base for raids into Mughal [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. His son [[e:damaji-rao-gaekwad|Damaji Rao II]] took Baroda ([[e:vadodara|Vadodara]]) and much of the province, and the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] became one of the great Maratha houses alongside the [[e:peshwa|Peshwas]], [[e:holkars|Holkars]] and [[e:scindias|Scindias]].
baroda-state.r: After disputed successions, Baroda entered a subsidiary alliance with the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] in 1802–05. In 1875 the British deposed [[e:malhar-rao-gaekwad|Malhar Rao]] for an alleged attempt to poison the Resident. His adopted successor [[e:sayajirao-gaekwad-iii|Sayajirao Gaekwad III]] (1875–1939) introduced compulsory primary education, a state library network, courts and railways, banned child marriage and funded scholars including [[e:b-r-ambedkar|B. R. Ambedkar]]. The state ranked among the few with a 21-gun salute.
baroda-state.e: [[e:pratapsinh-gaekwad|Pratapsinh Gaekwad]] acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947, and on 1 May 1949 Baroda was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]]; since 1960 it has been part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. The [[e:lakshmi-vilas-palace|Lakshmi Vilas Palace]] and the [[e:maharaja-sayajirao-university-of-baroda|Maharaja Sayajirao University]] are its best-known legacies.

bhavnagar-state.t: The Gohil Rajput port state of eastern Kathiawar whose last ruler was the first prince to hand his state over to the Indian people.
bhavnagar-state.o: The [[e:gohil|Gohil Rajputs]] had ruled in southern [[e:kathiawar|Saurashtra]] since the 13th century from [[e:sihor|Sihor]]. In 1723 [[e:bhavsinhji-i|Bhavsinhji I]] founded the port of Bhavnagar on the [[e:gulf-of-khambhat|Gulf of Khambhat]] and moved his capital there, giving the state its name. It was also known as Gohilwad after the ruling clan.
bhavnagar-state.r: Bhavnagar grew rich from sea trade, especially [[e:cotton|cotton]] exported to [[e:mumbai|Bombay]], and cooperated with the British against piracy in the Gulf. Under rulers such as [[e:takhtsinhji|Takhtsinhji]] it built railways, colleges and hospitals and was regarded as one of the better-administered states of the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]], with [[e:prabhashankar-pattani|Prabhashankar Pattani]] as a noted [[e:diwan|diwan]].
bhavnagar-state.e: In January 1948 Krishnakumarsinhji announced the transfer of power to a popular government, and Bhavnagar was merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948; it has been in [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] since 1960. Krishnakumarsinhji later served as Governor of [[e:chennai|Madras]].

cr.a: Dr. Andreas Birken at German Wikipedia

barbados.t: Easternmost Caribbean island, independent since 1966 and a parliamentary republic since 2021, with one of the region's oldest parliaments.
barbados.o: English settlers arrived in 1627, and Barbados became the first great [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and slave society of the English [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]], with a [[e:house-of-assembly-of-barbados|House of Assembly]] dating from 1639. After labour riots in 1937 and the rise of [[e:grantley-adams|Grantley Adams's]] [[e:barbados-labour-party|Barbados Labour Party]], it achieved self-government, and under [[e:errol-barrow|Errol Barrow]] of the [[e:democratic-labour-party-barbados|Democratic Labour Party]] it became independent on 30 November 1966.
barbados.r: For 55 years Barbados was a [[e:commonwealth-of-nations|Commonwealth]] realm with the British monarch as head of state. Power alternated peacefully between the [[e:democratic-labour-party-barbados|Democratic Labour Party]] and the [[e:barbados-labour-party|Barbados Labour Party]]. [[e:errol-barrow|Barrow]] and [[e:tom-adams|Tom Adams]] invested in education and health, and the economy shifted from [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] to tourism and offshore financial services, giving the island one of the highest living standards in the region.
barbados.e: On 30 November 2021 Barbados became a parliamentary republic, with [[e:sandra-mason|Sandra Mason]] as the first president and the singer [[e:rihanna|Rihanna]] named a national hero. Prime Minister [[e:mia-mottley|Mia Mottley]], in office since 2018, has promoted the [[e:bridgetown-initiative|Bridgetown Initiative]] on climate finance.

bijna-state.t: A tiny chiefship of the Bundelkhand Agency, one of the smallest polities recognised by the British in central India.
bijna-state.o: Bijna was recognised as a separate holding under British protection in the early 19th century, one of a number of small [[e:bundela|Bundela]] estates confirmed after the British gained supremacy in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]].
bijna-state.r: Little is recorded of its history; it consisted of a few villages under a hereditary chief supervised by the political agent in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]].
bijna-state.e: After independence Bijna was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states, and its lands were absorbed into the Indian administration by 1950.

bihwa-gaya.t: A Gaya statelet at Changnyeong on the Nakdong river, the first of the Gaya polities to fall under Silla's sway.
bihwa-gaya.o: Bihwa Gaya, called Bisabeol in [[s:silla|Silla]] records, developed from a Byeonhan-era community in the [[e:changnyeong-county|Changnyeong]] basin on the east bank of the [[e:nakdong-river|Nakdong]]. Its large mounded tombs at [[e:gyo-dong-and-songhyeon-dong-tombs|Gyo-dong]] and Songhyeon-dong date mainly from the 5th century.
bihwa-gaya.r: Little is recorded of its rulers. The tomb goods, including gilt-bronze crowns and stoneware in [[s:silla|Silla]] style, show that the local elite was drawn into Silla's orbit early while keeping its own burial grounds, and the polity served as a gateway between Silla and the western Gaya states.
bihwa-gaya.e: [[s:silla|Silla]] established a province at Bisabeol in 555 and [[e:jinheung-of-silla|King Jinheung]] erected a stele there in 561 recording his tour and naming his officials, marking the area's full incorporation. The tombs of [[e:gyo-dong-and-songhyeon-dong-tombs|Songhyeon-dong]] yielded a well-preserved sacrificed girl, reconstructed in 2008.

bechuanaland-protectorate.t: The British protectorate over the Tswana kingdoms, ruled from outside its own borders, which became independent Botswana.
bechuanaland-protectorate.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] declared a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] over the land north of the [[e:molopo-river|Molopo River]] in 1885, after the [[e:warren-expedition|Warren Expedition]], to block German and [[e:boers|Boer]] expansion and keep open the road to the interior. [[e:tswana-people|Tswana]] rulers such as [[e:khama-iii|Khama III]] of the [[s:bangwato-kingdom|Bangwato Kingdom]] welcomed protection against the Boers and the [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]].
bechuanaland-protectorate.r: Administration was minimal and ran from [[e:mahikeng|Mafeking]], outside the territory. In 1895 [[e:khama-iii|Khama III]], [[e:sebele-i|Sebele]] and [[e:bathoen-i|Bathoen]] travelled to [[e:london|London]] and persuaded the government not to hand them to [[e:cecil-rhodes|Cecil Rhodes's]] company. Chiefs kept wide powers, and many men worked in South African mines. The marriage of [[e:seretse-khama|Seretse Khama]] to a white Englishwoman in 1948 led [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] to exile him under South African pressure.
bechuanaland-protectorate.e: [[e:seretse-khama|Seretse Khama]] returned to lead the [[e:botswana-democratic-party|Bechuanaland Democratic Party]], which won the 1965 election. The territory became independent as [[e:botswana|Botswana]] on 30 September 1966, with a new capital at [[e:gaborone|Gaborone]] and Seretse Khama as president.

belgae-britain.t: Central southern British people around Winchester, whose name recalls the Belgae of northern Gaul and who formed a civitas of Roman Britain.
belgae-britain.o: [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] wrote that the coastal parts of [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] had been settled by Belgae from [[e:gaul|Gaul]] who kept their tribal names, and Belgic coins circulated widely in the south from the 2nd century BCE. A people called Belgae is named only from Roman times, however, and their pre-conquest identity is uncertain; [[e:winchester|Winchester]], the later [[e:venta-belgarum|Venta Belgarum]], had a late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] enclosure at Oram's Arbour.
belgae-britain.r: Before the conquest the region of [[e:hampshire|Hampshire]] and [[e:wiltshire|Wiltshire]] seems to have fallen within the sphere of the [[s:atrebates-britain|Atrebates (Britain)]] and their kings [[e:commius|Commius]], [[e:tincomarus|Tincomarus]] and [[e:verica|Verica]], sharing their coinage and links with [[e:gaul|Gaul]]. Farming was rich on the chalk downs, and hillforts such as [[e:danebury|Danebury]] had been major storage centres in earlier centuries.
belgae-britain.e: After 43 the area may first have been part of the realm of [[e:togidubnus|Togidubnus]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-regni|Kingdom of the Regni]]. On his death it was organised as the civitas of the Belgae, with [[e:venta-belgarum|Venta Belgarum]] as its capital; Ptolemy also lists [[e:bath|Aquae Sulis]], Bath, among their towns. [[e:winchester|Winchester]] later became the royal seat of [[s:kingdom-of-wessex|Wessex]].

bremen-verden.t: Two secularised prince-bishoprics between the Elbe and Weser that Sweden ruled as duchies from 1648 until losing them to Denmark and Hanover.
bremen-verden.o: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 turned the [[s:prince-archbishopric-of-bremen|Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen]] and the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-verden|Prince-Bishopric of Verden]] into secular duchies and granted them to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] as imperial fiefs. The Swedish crown thus gained a seat in the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]] and control of the mouths of the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and [[e:weser|Weser]].
bremen-verden.r: [[e:sweden|Sweden]] governed the duchies from [[e:stade|Stade]], which it fortified, through a governor-general and the local estates. The city of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] claimed to be a free imperial city, and Sweden fought two wars against it in 1654 and 1666 without subduing it. The lands were mainly marsh and heath farming country with a Lutheran population.
bremen-verden.e: During the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]] [[e:denmark|Denmark]] occupied the duchies in 1712. Denmark sold them in 1715 to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]], whose elector was also [[e:george-i-of-great-britain|George I of Great Britain]], and [[e:sweden|Sweden]] ceded them formally in 1719. They later formed part of [[e:hanover|Hanover]] and of the German state of [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

bonapartist-spain.t: The Spanish kingdom of Joseph Bonaparte, imposed by Napoleon in 1808 and swept away by the Peninsular War.
bonapartist-spain.o: In 1808 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] summoned Charles IV and his son [[e:ferdinand-vii-of-spain|Ferdinand VII]] to [[e:bayonne|Bayonne]] and forced both to abdicate. He gave the throne to his brother Joseph, who was proclaimed Joseph I and granted the [[e:statute-of-bayonne|Statute of Bayonne]], [[e:spain|Spain's]] first constitution, while the [[e:madrid|Madrid]] rising of 2 May was brutally suppressed.
bonapartist-spain.r: Joseph's government, supported by reformist afrancesados, abolished the [[e:portuguese-inquisition|Inquisition]], seigneurial rights and many convents. But it depended entirely on French armies and never controlled the whole country. Patriot juntas, the [[e:cortes-of-cadiz|Cortes of Cádiz]] with its Constitution of 1812, [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]] and [[e:wellington|Wellington's]] Anglo-Portuguese army fought it throughout the [[e:peninsular-war|Peninsular War]].
bonapartist-spain.e: After the defeat at Vitoria in June 1813 Joseph left [[e:spain|Spain]]. By the [[e:treaty-of-valencay|Treaty of Valençay]] in December 1813 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] restored [[e:ferdinand-vii-of-spain|Ferdinand VII]], returning the country to [[s:bourbon-spain|Bourbon Spain]].

barony-of-akova.t: Frankish barony in the hills of western Arcadia, centred on the castle the French called Matagrifon, lost to the Byzantines in 1320.
barony-of-akova.o: The barony of [[e:akova|Akova]] was among the twelve original baronies of the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]], created around 1209 and granted to [[e:walter-of-rosieres|Walter of Rosieres]], with 24 knight's fiefs. Its castle in the mountains between [[s:elis|Elis]] and [[e:arcadia|Arcadia]] was called Matagrifon, 'kill the [[e:greeks|Greeks]]', reflecting its role in holding down the region.
barony-of-akova.r: The barons owed service to the prince and sat in his high court. After the Rosieres line died out, the inheritance of [[e:margaret-of-passavant|Margaret of Passavant]] to [[e:akova|Akova]] was disputed in the 1270s, a famous case recorded in the [[e:chronicle-of-the-morea|Chronicle of the Morea]] and in the [[e:assizes-of-romania|Assizes of Romania]], and much of the barony passed to the princely domain.
barony-of-akova.e: In 1320 the Byzantine governor [[e:andronikos-asen|Andronikos Asen]] captured [[e:akova|Akova]] along with [[e:karytaina|Karytaina]] and other castles of central [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]], bringing the barony into what became the [[s:despotate-of-the-morea|Despotate of the Morea]].

british-occupation-of-saint-domingue.t: Britain's costly five-year attempt to seize revolutionary Saint-Domingue, which cost it tens of thousands of soldiers, mostly to yellow fever.
british-occupation-of-saint-domingue.o: Royalist French planters, alarmed by the abolition of [[e:slavery|slavery]], invited [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] to take over [[s:saint-domingue|Saint-Domingue]] after war broke out with revolutionary [[e:france|France]]. British troops from [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]] landed at [[e:jeremie|Jérémie]] and [[e:mole-saint-nicolas|Môle Saint-Nicolas]] in September 1793 and captured [[e:port-au-prince|Port-au-Prince]] in June 1794.
british-occupation-of-saint-domingue.r: The occupiers governed the coastal towns they held in alliance with planters and with restored [[e:slavery|slavery]], relying heavily on locally raised black and coloured troops. They never controlled the interior. Yellow fever and malaria devastated the reinforcements sent from [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], while [[e:toussaint-louverture|Toussaint Louverture]], now fighting for the [[s:french-fifth-republic|French Republic]], and [[e:andre-rigaud|André Rigaud]] pressed them from the north and south.
british-occupation-of-saint-domingue.e: With losses mounting, Brigadier [[e:thomas-maitland|Thomas Maitland]] negotiated an evacuation with [[e:toussaint-louverture|Toussaint]] and withdrew the last British forces in 1798, also reaching a secret trade agreement. The failure helped Toussaint consolidate power and strengthened the path to Haitian independence.

bangkalan-kingdom.t: West Madurese realm of the Cakraningrat dynasty, first a vassal of Mataram and then a key Dutch ally on the island of Madura.
bangkalan-kingdom.o: After [[e:sultan-agung|Sultan Agung]] of the [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram Sultanate]] conquered [[e:madura|Madura]] in 1624, he installed a local prince, Raden Praseno, as Cakraningrat I to rule the western half of the island from [[e:sampang|Sampang]]. The dynasty owed loyalty to Mataram, but its Madurese subjects were restless, and the prince [[e:trunajaya|Trunajaya]] led a great rebellion against Mataram from 1674 to 1680.
bangkalan-kingdom.r: The Cakraningrat princes ruled a dry island of salt pans, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and fishing whose men served as soldiers across [[e:java|Java]]. [[e:cakraningrat-iv|Cakraningrat IV]] turned against [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]] and the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] in the 1740s and was exiled to the Cape in 1745. His successors moved the court to Bangkalan and became firm Company allies.
bangkalan-kingdom.e: Bangkalan troops served the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] in [[e:java|Java]] and beyond, and in the early 19th century its rulers received the title of sultan. The Dutch gradually reduced their powers and abolished the kingdom in 1885, placing West [[e:madura|Madura]] under direct colonial rule as part of the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]].

british-mauritius.t: The sugar island taken from France in 1810, transformed by Indian indentured labour into a mainly Indian-descended society.
british-mauritius.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] seized the French [[s:isle-de-france|Isle de France]] in December 1810, landing at [[e:cap-malheureux|Cap Malheureux]] months after a French naval victory at [[e:grand-port|Grand Port]], in order to stop French raiders preying on [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]] shipping. The island was ceded in the 1814 [[e:treaty-of-paris-1814|Treaty of Paris]], renamed [[e:mauritius|Mauritius]], and its first governor, [[e:robert-townsend-farquhar|Robert Farquhar]], ruled from [[e:port-louis|Port Louis]].
british-mauritius.r: The capitulation let Franco-Mauritian planters keep their French law, language and Catholic church, and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] became the island's economy. After [[e:slavery|slavery]] ended in 1835, nearly half a million indentured labourers arrived from [[e:india|India]] through the immigration depot now called [[e:aapravasi-ghat|Aapravasi Ghat]], so that [[e:hinduism|Hindus]] and Muslims of Indian origin became the majority while [[e:criollo-people|Creoles]] and French-speaking whites kept much economic power.
british-mauritius.e: After constitutional reforms and the rise of the Labour Party, [[e:mauritius|Mauritius]] became independent on 12 March 1968 under [[e:seewoosagur-ramgoolam|Seewoosagur Ramgoolam]], and a republic in 1992. The [[e:chagos-archipelago|Chagos Archipelago]], detached by [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1965, remained disputed.

cr.a: Orange Tuesday Original uploader was Orange Tuesday at en.wikipedia

buyeo.t: A kingdom of the Manchurian plains that Goguryeo and Baekje both claimed as their ancestral homeland, and a long-time ally of Han China.
buyeo.o: Buyeo appears in Chinese sources in the 2nd century BCE as a farming and herding kingdom on the [[e:songhua-river|Songhua]] river plain around modern [[e:jilin-city|Jilin]]. Its founding legend of [[e:dongmyeong-of-buyeo|Dongmyeong]], born of sunlight and escaping across a river on a bridge of fish and turtles, was later borrowed for the founder of [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]].
buyeo.r: The king shared power with four great officials named after animals: horse, ox, pig and dog, each governing a region. Kings could be blamed and deposed for bad harvests. Laws were strict, the yeonggo festival in the twelfth month honoured heaven, and nobles were buried with human victims. Buyeo usually sided with Chinese dynasties against [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] and the [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]].
buyeo.e: [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] raids under the [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong]] in 285 and 346 devastated the kingdom, and King [[e:uiryeo-of-buyeo|Uiryeo]] took his own life in the first. Weakened and pressed by the [[e:mohe|Mohe]], the last king surrendered to [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] in 494. Baekje's later name [[s:baekje|Nambuyeo]] recalled the link.

bit-yakin.t: The most powerful Chaldean tribe of southern Babylonia, home of Merodach-baladan, the long-time rival of the kings of Assyria.
bit-yakin.o: Bit-Yakin occupied the marshes and coastland at the head of the Gulf, the region once called the [[s:sealand-dynasty|Sealand]]. Its fortified centre was Dur-Yakin. Like the other [[e:chaldean-tribes|Chaldean tribes]], it appears in Assyrian annals in the 9th century BCE, when its chiefs paid tribute to [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]].
bit-yakin.r: Its sheikhs grew rich from date palms, Gulf trade and control of the marsh routes, which also made their land a refuge from Assyrian armies. [[e:merodach-baladan-ii|Merodach-baladan II]] (Marduk-apla-iddina) made himself king of [[e:babylon|Babylon]] from 721 to 710 BCE and again in 703 BCE, allied with the [[s:neo-elamite-kingdom|Neo-Elamite kingdom]] and sent envoys as far as [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]], an embassy mentioned in the Bible.
bit-yakin.e: [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] took Dur-Yakin in 709 BCE, and [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib]] pursued the tribe's refugees by ship to [[e:elam|Elam]] in 694 BCE. [[e:merodach-baladan-ii|Merodach-baladan]]'s grandson Nabu-bel-shumati joined [[e:shamash-shum-ukin|Shamash-shum-ukin's]] revolt and died in Elam around 648 BCE, after which Bit-Yakin disappears as a power.

baudh-state.t: A princely state on the upper Mahanadi in Odisha, whose capital Boudh holds Buddhist and Hindu remains, ruled by Rajas until 1948.
baudh-state.o: Tradition places the founding of the ruling dynasty around 1400. The town's name is linked to the Buddhist remains found there, including a large seated Buddha image.
baudh-state.r: Baudh was an inland state of farmland and forest on the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]]. It was linked with the neighbouring [[e:kondh|Kondh]] hill tracts, which were separated from it under British rule in the 19th century. It paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and later belonged to the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary States]]. Its internal history is poorly documented.
baudh-state.e: Baudh merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now Boudh district, Odisha.

bellovaci.t: The most powerful of the Belgic peoples, around Beauvais, who fought Caesar in 57 BCE and led one of the last Gallic revolts in 51 BCE.
bellovaci.o: The Bellovaci lived in the modern [[e:oise-department|Oise]] and [[e:picardy|Picardy]] around [[e:beauvais|Beauvais]]. Caesar was told that they could field a hundred thousand men and had promised sixty thousand to the Belgic league of 57 BCE.
bellovaci.r: Their society was led by a warrior nobility, and they had ties to the [[s:aedui|Aedui]]. Large sanctuaries such as [[e:gournay-sur-aronde|Gournay-sur-Aronde]], with displays of weapons and sacrificed animals, show their religious practice.
bellovaci.e: In 57 BCE they surrendered at [[e:bratuspantium|Bratuspantium]] after the Aeduan [[e:diviciacus-aedui|Diviciacus]] spoke for them. In 51 BCE they rose under [[e:correus|Correus]], who died fighting. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town became [[e:beauvais|Caesaromagus]], later Beauvais.

cr.a: The Department of History, United States Military Academy

bhaisaunda-state.t: One of the Chaube jagirs near Kalinjar in Bundelkhand, granted to the Brahmin family that surrendered the fort to the British in 1812.
bhaisaunda-state.o: Bhaisaunda was one of the small holdings given in 1812 to members of the Chaube family, [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] governors of [[e:kalinjar-fort|Kalinjar]] fort under the rulers of [[s:panna-state|Panna]], when they handed the fortress over to the British.
bhaisaunda-state.r: It was a minor estate of a few villages under the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]]. Little else of its history is recorded.
bhaisaunda-state.e: After independence Bhaisaunda was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states and absorbed by 1950.

beirut.t: Beirut, a Late Bronze Age Canaanite port known from the Amarna letters, ancestor of the modern Lebanese capital.
beirut.o: Biruta grew on a promontory on the central Lebanese coast, settled since prehistory. By the 15th century BCE it was a small walled port town under the overlordship of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]].
beirut.r: Its ruler [[e:ammunira|Ammunira]] wrote to the [[e:pharaoh|pharaoh]] in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]], promising loyalty and sending reports. When [[e:rib-hadda|Rib-Hadda]] of [[s:byblos|Byblos]] was driven out of his city by a rebellion, he took refuge in Beirut. Excavations in the city centre after the civil war uncovered its [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]] walls.
beirut.e: The Canaanite town shared the decline of the coast in the 12th century BCE, and in the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] remained in the shadow of [[s:sidon|Sidon]] and [[s:tyre|Tyre]]. It later grew into the Roman colony of Berytus.

banu-khurasan.t: A local dynasty that ruled Tunis as an independent city-state after the Zirid collapse, until the Almohad conquest.
banu-khurasan.o: After the [[e:banu-hilal|Banu Hilal]] defeated the [[s:zirid-emirate|Zirid emirate]] and [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] was abandoned in 1057, [[e:tunis|Tunis]] broke away. Around 1059 its notables chose Abd al-Haqq ibn Abd [[e:al-aziz|al-Aziz]] ibn [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]], from a local family of notables, as ruler, founding the Khurasanid dynasty in the old port city.
banu-khurasan.r: The Khurasanids ruled [[e:tunis|Tunis]] and its hinterland as a small [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] city-state, at first recognising the [[s:hammadid-emirate|Hammadid emirate]] as overlord to secure protection from the Arab tribes and the [[e:zirid-dynasty|Zirids of Mahdia]]. They paid the [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] for peace, strengthened the walls and encouraged trade by sea. Ahmad ibn Abd [[e:al-aziz|al-Aziz]], the most notable ruler, built palaces and gathered scholars at his court.
banu-khurasan.e: The dynasty was briefly displaced by the [[s:hammadid-emirate|Hammadids]] in 1128, but returned. In 1159 the [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohad]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:abd-al-mumin|Abd al-Mu'min]] took [[e:tunis|Tunis]], ending its independence, and the city later became the capital of the [[s:hafsid-sultanate|Hafsids]].

bit-hamban.t: A Zagros principality on the great road from Mesopotamia into Iran, repeatedly raided and finally annexed by Assyria.
bit-hamban.o: Bit-Hamban lay in the western [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]], probably around the upper [[e:diyala-river|Diyala]] and the [[e:kermanshah|Kermanshah]] region, along the route later called the Great [[e:khorasan|Khorasan]] Road. It appears in Assyrian annals from the reign of [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] in the mid-9th century BCE as a land of local lords.
bit-hamban.r: Nothing is known of its institutions beyond Assyrian campaign reports, which list towns captured and tribute of horses and livestock. Its rulers seem to have been local chiefs rather than kings of a centralised state, sometimes in league with neighbours such as [[s:parsua|Parsua]] and [[s:ellipi|Ellipi]].
bit-hamban.e: Tiglath-Pileser III incorporated Bit-Hamban into the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] in 744 BCE, and under [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] it formed part of the Assyrian provincial system in the [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]]. It disappears from the record by about 700 BCE.

berar-sultanate.t: The smallest of the Deccan sultanates, ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty from Ellichpur in the Berar plain of central India.
berar-sultanate.o: [[e:fathullah-imad-ul-mulk|Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk]], a Bahmani governor of [[e:berar|Berar]] who was originally a [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] convert from [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara]] territory, declared independence around 1490 as the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]] broke up. He ruled from [[e:achalpur|Ellichpur]] and the fort of [[e:gawilgarh|Gawilgarh]], founding the [[e:imad-shahi-dynasty|Imad Shahi dynasty]].
berar-sultanate.r: [[e:berar|Berar]] was a fertile [[e:cotton|cotton]] and grain-growing region, but the sultanate was weak and survived by balancing between its neighbours, the [[s:ahmadnagar-sultanate|Ahmadnagar Sultanate]], the [[s:khandesh-sultanate|Khandesh Sultanate]] and the [[s:bijapur-sultanate|Bijapur Sultanate]]. Its rulers strengthened the hill fortresses of [[e:gawilgarh|Gawilgarh]] and [[e:narnala|Narnala]]. Few literary sources describe its internal history.
berar-sultanate.e: [[e:murtaza-nizam-shah-i|Murtaza Nizam Shah]] of the [[s:ahmadnagar-sultanate|Ahmadnagar Sultanate]] invaded [[e:berar|Berar]] and annexed it in 1574, ending the [[e:imad-shahi-dynasty|Imad Shahi]] line. Berar later passed to the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]], then to the [[e:nizam-of-hyderabad|Nizams of Hyderabad]] and finally the British.

bhadva-state.t: A minor chiefship of the Kathiawar peninsula, one of its many small hereditary estates.
bhadva-state.o: Bhadva was a small estate in [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a local [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family from around 1700. Its founding is not well documented.
bhadva-state.r: The ruler held a few villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Few further details are recorded in standard works.
bhadva-state.e: Bhadva merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in [[s:rajkot-state|Rajkot]] district.

batavi.t: Germanic people of the Rhine delta who served as Rome's elite soldiers and imperial bodyguards, then rose in a great revolt in 69 CE.
batavi.o: [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] says the Batavi were a branch of the [[s:chatti|Chatti]] who, after a quarrel at home, settled on the island between the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] and the [[e:waal|Waal]], the modern [[e:betuwe|Betuwe]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]], probably in the later 1st century BCE.
batavi.r: Instead of paying tribute, they supplied [[e:rome|Rome]] with soldiers: cavalry famous for swimming rivers in full armour, auxiliary [[e:cohort|cohorts]] and the emperors' German bodyguard. Their noble families commanded these units, and their chief town [[e:batavodurum|Batavodurum]] stood at [[e:nijmegen|Nijmegen]].
batavi.e: In 69 CE [[e:julius-civilis|Julius Civilis]] led a revolt joined by the [[s:cananefates|Cananefates]], [[s:frisii|Frisii]] and [[s:treveri|Treveri]], which was crushed in 70 CE. The Batavi resumed service, and [[e:nijmegen|Ulpia Noviomagus]] (Nijmegen) became a Roman town. They faded in the Frankish period, but the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] long saw them as ancestors.

bijawar-state.t: A Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand, founded in the 1760s by a descendant of Chhatrasal.
bijawar-state.o: Bijawar was founded around 1765 by Bir Singh Deo, a [[e:bundela|Bundela]] of the family of [[e:chhatrasal|Chhatrasal]], who carved out his own territory as Bundela power fragmented.
bijawar-state.r: The British confirmed the state by sanad in the early 19th century. Bijawar was an 11-gun salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]], ruled by a [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] over a hilly, partly forested territory. Little else of its internal history is recorded.
bijawar-state.e: After independence Bijawar was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] and absorbed by 1950; it is now in [[s:chhatarpur-state|Chhatarpur]] district of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]].

black-sea-cossack-host.t: A Cossack army formed from former Zaporozhians, which settled the Kuban frontier and founded the city now called Krasnodar.
black-sea-cossack-host.o: In 1787, on the eve of war with the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], Prince [[e:grigory-potemkin|Grigory Potemkin]] gathered former [[e:zaporozhian-cossacks|Zaporozhian Cossacks]] into the [[e:host-of-loyal-zaporozhians|Host of Loyal Zaporozhians]]. Led by [[e:sydir-bilyi|Sydir Bilyi]], [[e:zakhary-chepiha|Zakhary Chepiha]] and [[e:anton-holovaty|Anton Holovaty]], they fought at [[e:ochakiv|Ochakiv]] and [[e:izmail|Izmail]], and in 1790 they were renamed the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] Host.
black-sea-cossack-host.r: In 1792 [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine II]] granted the Host the lands of the Taman peninsula and the right bank of the Kuban, and in 1793 they founded [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]] as their capital. The [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] kept elected officers and a Zaporozhian tradition, farming and guarding a fortified line against the [[e:circassians|Circassians]] across the Kuban.
black-sea-cossack-host.e: The Host fought throughout the [[e:caucasian-war|Caucasian War]]. In 1860 it was merged with part of the [[e:caucasus-line-cossack-host|Caucasus Line Cossack Host]] to form the [[s:kuban-cossack-host|Kuban Cossack Host]]. Its Ukrainian heritage shaped the speech and culture of the Kuban region.

bondelswarts.t: A Nama community of southern Namibia centred on Warmbad, known for its uprisings against German and later South African rule.
bondelswarts.o: The Bondelswarts, in [[e:nama-people|Nama]] !Gami-ǂnun, were a Khoekhoe-speaking Nama group living north of the [[e:orange-river|Orange River]]. In 1805 the [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] founded a mission at [[e:warmbad|Warmbad]] among them, and [[e:methodism|Wesleyans]] took it over in the 1830s; Warmbad became the seat of their kapteins.
bondelswarts.r: Like other [[e:nama-people|Nama]] communities they were governed by a hereditary kaptein, here of the Christian family, with a council of elders. They lived by herding [[e:cattle|cattle]], sheep and goats in the dry south, traded with the Cape and many adopted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and [[e:cape-dutch|Cape Dutch]] through the mission.
bondelswarts.e: In 1903 the killing of their kaptein [[e:jan-abraham-christian|Jan Abraham Christian]] by German officials sparked a rising, which merged into the wider [[e:nama-people|Nama]] war; they made peace at Ukamas in December 1906 and lost most of their land. Their 1922 rebellion against a South African dog tax was crushed with aircraft.

byzacena.t: The late Roman province of central Tunisia, an olive-growing land of prosperous towns governed from Hadrumetum.
byzacena.o: Around 303 [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]] divided [[s:africa-proconsularis|Africa Proconsularis]] into smaller provinces as part of his reorganisation of the empire. The southern part of the old province, the region known as Byzacium, became Byzacena, with its capital at [[e:sousse|Hadrumetum]] (Sousse), and was governed by a consularis within the Diocese of [[e:africa|Africa]].
byzacena.r: Byzacena was one of the richest farming regions of the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]], covered with olive groves whose oil was shipped to [[e:rome|Rome]] and beyond. Towns such as [[e:el-djem|Thysdrus]], with its great amphitheatre at El Djem, [[e:sufetula|Sufetula]] and [[e:thaenae|Thaenae]] flourished. The province had many bishoprics and was strongly affected by the [[e:donatism|Donatist]] controversy. Large imperial and private estates employed tenant farmers, the coloni.
byzacena.e: The [[e:vandals|Vandals]] took control after capturing [[e:carthage|Carthage]] in 439, and the region was part of the [[s:vandal-kingdom|Vandal Kingdom]] until Justinian's reconquest in 534 restored a province of Byzacena under the [[s:praetorian-prefecture-of-africa|Praetorian Prefecture of Africa]]. [[e:berbers|Berber]] kingdoms such as the [[s:kingdom-of-capsus|Kingdom of Capsus]] held its southern edges.

bailiwick-of-guernsey.t: A self-governing British Crown Dependency of Channel Islands, held by the crown as heir of the Dukes of Normandy since 1204.
bailiwick-of-guernsey.o: Guernsey belonged to the [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Duchy of Normandy]] from the 10th century. When [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] lost continental Normandy to [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II of France]] in 1204, the islands stayed with the English crown, and a separate bailiwick, under its own bailiff and royal court, developed for Guernsey, [[s:alderney|Alderney]], [[s:sark|Sark]] and the smaller islands.
bailiwick-of-guernsey.r: Guernsey kept Norman customary law, its Royal Court of jurats and, later, the [[e:states-of-deliberation|States of Deliberation]] as its parliament. Its economy rested on fishing, knitting, privateering and later [[e:tomato|tomatoes]], horticulture and finance. [[e:saint-peter-port|Saint Peter Port]] was a major harbour. During the [[e:english-civil-war|English Civil War]] it sided with Parliament, and [[e:victor-hugo|Victor Hugo]] lived there in exile from 1855.
bailiwick-of-guernsey.e: Guernsey was occupied by [[e:germany|Germany]] from 1940 to 1945. Today it is a [[e:crown-dependencies|Crown Dependency]], not part of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-ireland|United Kingdom]], with its own government, laws and taxes, while the UK handles defence and international relations.

bamra-state.t: A princely state of the Sambalpur hills in western Odisha whose 19th-century Raja made its capital Deogarh a centre of Odia printing and literature.
bamra-state.o: The ruling family claimed descent from the [[s:eastern-ganga-dynasty|Eastern Ganga dynasty]], and tradition dates the state to the mid-16th century. It was one of the chiefships in the orbit of [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur State]].
bamra-state.r: Bamra, also called Bamanda, was a hilly, forested state. It came under the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]] and later British supervision. Raja Basudeb Sudhal Deb (r. 1869–1903) set up a [[e:printing-press|printing]] press at [[e:deogarh-odisha|Deogarh]] that published an [[e:odia-language|Odia]] newspaper and books, and introduced schools and public works.
bamra-state.e: Bamra merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948, and [[e:deogarh-odisha|Deogarh]] is now the headquarters of Deogarh district.

cr.a: Govern britànic de l'Índia / Government of British India

baluchistan-states-union.t: A short-lived federation of the four princely states of Balochistan within Pakistan, led by the Khan of Kalat.
baluchistan-states-union.o: In 1952 [[s:khanate-of-kalat|Kalat]], [[s:kharan-state|Kharan]], [[s:makran-state|Makran State]] and [[s:las-bela-state|Las Bela State]], which had acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1948, were combined into the [[e:balochistan|Baluchistan]] States Union. The Khan of Kalat, [[e:ahmad-yar-khan|Ahmad Yar Khan]], became its head as Khan-e-Azam.
baluchistan-states-union.r: The union had a council of the rulers and a small administration based at [[s:khanate-of-kalat|Kalat]], with [[e:pakistan|Pakistan's]] government retaining control of defence, foreign affairs and communications. It covered a vast, thinly populated territory of pastoralists, farmers and coastal fishermen.
baluchistan-states-union.e: In 1955 the union was dissolved and merged into [[e:west-pakistan|West Pakistan]] under the One Unit scheme, ending the political role of the [[e:baloch-people|Baloch]] rulers. Its lands are now part of [[e:balochistan|Balochistan]] province.

balearic-islanders.t: The tower-building peoples of Mallorca and Menorca, whose stone talaiots and taulas still dot the islands and whose slingers fought for Carthage and Rome.
balearic-islanders.o: From around 1000 BCE the islanders of [[e:mallorca|Mallorca]] and [[e:menorca|Menorca]] developed what archaeologists call the Talaiotic culture, named after the talaiots, massive [[e:dry-stone-construction|dry-stone]] towers that dominated fortified villages. It grew out of the earlier Naviform culture of boat-shaped houses and stone tombs such as the [[e:naveta-des-tudons|Naveta des Tudons]] on Menorca.
balearic-islanders.r: There was no single state: the islands were divided among village communities, probably led by local chiefs, living from herding, farming and some trade with Phoenician and Punic merchants, especially from nearby [[s:ebusus|Ebusus]]. [[e:menorca|Menorca's]] T-shaped taulas stood in sanctuary enclosures. The islanders were famed throughout the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] as slingers and served as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] in Carthaginian armies, including [[e:hannibal|Hannibal's]].
balearic-islanders.e: Accused of sheltering [[e:piracy|pirates]], the islands were conquered in 123 BCE by the Roman general [[e:quintus-caecilius-metellus-balearicus|Quintus Caecilius Metellus]], who took the name Balearicus and founded the towns of [[e:palma|Palma]] and [[e:pollentia|Pollentia]]. Talaiotic traditions faded under Roman rule, but hundreds of monuments survive.

burgraviate-of-nuremberg.t: The castle office at Nuremberg that gave the Hohenzollerns their first foothold in Franconia, the start of their rise to kings of Prussia.
burgraviate-of-nuremberg.o: Around 1105 the Salian emperors appointed burgraves to command the royal castle of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]]. The first family, the [[e:house-of-raabs|Raabs]], died out around 1190, and Frederick of [[s:county-of-hohenzollern|Zollern]], a Swabian noble married to the [[e:raba|Raabs]]' heiress, became burgrave in 1192, founding the [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Franconian Hohenzollern]] line.
burgraviate-of-nuremberg.r: The burgraves held the castle, rights of justice and lands around [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]], and gradually built a territory in [[e:franconia|Franconia]], acquiring [[s:principality-of-brandenburg-ansbach|Ansbach]] in 1331 and [[e:kulmbach|Kulmbach]] and [[e:bayreuth|Bayreuth]]. [[e:frederick-iii-of-nuremberg|Frederick III of Nuremberg]] helped elect Rudolf I in 1273. The city of [[e:nuremberg|Nuremberg]] itself grew into a free imperial city and rival.
burgraviate-of-nuremberg.e: In 1415 [[e:frederick-i-elector-of-brandenburg|Burgrave Frederick VI]] received the [[s:margraviate-of-brandenburg|Margraviate of Brandenburg]] as Elector Frederick I. In 1427 he sold the burgrave's castle to the city of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]]. His Franconian lands became the margraviates of [[e:brandenburg-ansbach|Brandenburg-Ansbach]] and [[s:principality-of-brandenburg-bayreuth|Brandenburg-Kulmbach]] ([[e:bayreuth|Bayreuth]]).

bessi.t: Thracian highland people of the Rhodopes and Haemus, keepers of a famous oracle of Dionysus and stubborn rebels against Rome.
bessi.o: [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]], writing in the 5th century BCE, names the Bessi as the priests of the oracle of [[e:dionysus|Dionysus]] in the mountains of the [[e:satrae|Satrae]]. By later centuries they were a distinct people of the upper [[e:maritsa|Hebrus]] (Maritsa) and [[e:rhodope-mountains|Rhodope]] ranges in modern [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]].
bessi.r: A loose tribal people of mountain country, the Bessi combined herding, mining and raiding. Their religious standing as guardians of the Dionysian sanctuary gave them prestige among [[e:thracians|Thracians]]. They clashed with the [[s:odrysian-kingdom|Odrysian Kingdom]] and with [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]], and later raided [[e:macedonia-roman-province|Roman Macedonia]].
bessi.e: [[e:marcus-licinius-crassus|Marcus Licinius Crassus]] subdued them in 29 BCE, but in 11 BCE the priest [[e:vologases-thracian-priest|Vologases]] led a major revolt that took years to crush. Their name survived under [[e:rome|Rome]], and a Bessian language was reportedly still used in monastic worship in the 6th century CE.

baria-state.t: A Chauhan Rajput state in eastern Gujarat founded by descendants of the last Rajput rulers of Champaner after its fall to the Gujarat Sultanate.
baria-state.o: When [[e:mahmud-begada|Mahmud Begada]] of the [[s:gujarat-sultanate|Gujarat Sultanate]] took [[e:champaner|Champaner]] and [[e:pavagadh|Pavagadh]] in 1484, the defeated [[e:chauhan|Chauhan Rajput]] rulers' descendants withdrew into the hills to the east. By tradition they founded Devgadh Baria in 1524, and it became the capital of their state.
baria-state.r: Baria was a forested, hilly state with a large [[e:bhils|Bhil]] population. It paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and later came under British supervision in the [[e:rewa-kantha-agency|Rewa Kantha Agency]]. Its later rulers built a palace and introduced modern administration in the early 20th century.
baria-state.e: Baria merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948. Its last ruler, Jaideepsinhji, later served as a minister in [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. Devgadh Baria is now in [[e:dahod|Dahod]] district.

bakwena-chiefdom.t: The Tswana chiefdom of the Kwena, whose ruler Sechele I was David Livingstone's only convert and a shrewd defender of his people.
bakwena-chiefdom.o: The [[e:bakwena|Bakwena]] trace their origin to a split from the [[e:bahurutshe|Bahurutshe]] and later gave rise to the [[e:bamangwato|Bangwato]] and [[e:bangwaketse|Bangwaketse]] through further divisions. By the 18th century the Kwena were settled in what is now south-eastern [[e:botswana|Botswana]], though they were scattered during the wars of the 1820s.
bakwena-chiefdom.r: [[e:sechele-i|Sechele I]] rebuilt the chiefdom from the 1830s, ruling through the kgotla and ward system. He welcomed [[e:david-livingstone|David Livingstone]], was baptised in 1848, and kept trade routes open to the north. In 1852 [[s:south-african-republic|Transvaal]] [[e:boers|Boers]] attacked his town at Dimawe, but Sechele survived and made the [[e:bakwena|Kwena]] a regional power, settling at [[e:molepolole|Molepolole]] in the 1860s.
bakwena-chiefdom.e: Fearing [[e:boers|Boer]] expansion, the [[e:tswana-people|Tswana]] chiefs accepted British protection, and in 1885 [[e:kweneng-district|Kweneng]] became part of the [[s:bechuanaland-protectorate|Bechuanaland Protectorate]]. The chiefdom continued under colonial rule and is part of independent [[e:botswana|Botswana]].

banu-ghaniya-majorca.t: The last Almoravid state, ruled from Majorca by the Banu Ghaniya, who waged a long war against the Almohads from the Balearics to Ifriqiya.
banu-ghaniya-majorca.o: Muhammad ibn [[e:ali-ibn-ghaniya|Ali ibn Ghaniya]], of an Almoravid family related to the ruling dynasty, governed the [[e:balearic-islands|Balearic Islands]] from about 1126. When the [[s:almoravid-empire|Almoravid Empire]] collapsed in the 1140s, he kept the islands as an independent [[e:emirate|emirate]] loyal to the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliph]].
banu-ghaniya-majorca.r: Under [[e:ishaq-ibn-ghaniya|Ishaq ibn Muhammad]] (c. 1155-1183) [[e:mallorca|Majorca]] prospered on trade and corsair raids, and made treaties with [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] and [[e:pisa|Pisa]]. In 1184 [[e:ali-ibn-ghaniya|Ali ibn Ghaniya]] invaded [[e:north-africa|North Africa]], seizing [[e:bejaia|Bejaia]] and starting a war against the [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohads]] in [[e:ifriqiya|Ifriqiya]] that lasted half a century.
banu-ghaniya-majorca.e: The [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohads]] conquered [[e:mallorca|Majorca]] in 1203, killing its ruler [[e:abd-allah-ibn-ishaq|Abd Allah ibn Ishaq]], though the family fought on in [[e:ifriqiya|Ifriqiya]]. [[e:james-i-of-aragon|James I of Aragon]] took Majorca in 1229, later forming the [[s:kingdom-of-majorca|Kingdom of Majorca]].

bukharan-peoples-soviet-republic.t: The Soviet-backed republic established after the Red Army stormed Bukhara in 1920, led by the Young Bukharan reformer Fayzulla Khodzhayev.
bukharan-peoples-soviet-republic.o: In September 1920 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] under [[e:mikhail-frunze|Mikhail Frunze]], supporting a revolt by the [[e:young-bukharans|Young Bukharans]] and Bukharan communists, captured [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] and drove out the last emir. The Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was proclaimed in October 1920.
bukharan-peoples-soviet-republic.r: Led by [[e:fayzulla-khodzhayev|Fayzulla Khodzhayev]] as chairman of the council of people's nazirs, the republic carried out land and educational reforms but remained dependent on Soviet troops and money. It faced the Basmachi resistance, which in 1921 and 1922 was joined by the Ottoman general [[e:enver-pasha|Enver Pasha]], killed in eastern [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] in 1922. It became the Bukharan Soviet Socialist Republic in 1924.
bukharan-peoples-soviet-republic.e: In the national delimitation of 1924 its territory was divided between the [[s:uzbek-ssr|Uzbek SSR]], the [[s:tajik-assr|Tajik ASSR]] and the [[s:turkmen-ssr|Turkmen SSR]]. Khodzhayev became head of the [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] government and was executed in 1938.

bastar-state.t: A vast forest kingdom in central India founded by refugees from the Kakatiya court, famous for its goddess Danteshwari and its 75-day Dussehra festival.
bastar-state.o: By tradition, [[e:annama-deva|Annama Deva]], a brother of the last Kakatiya king [[e:prataparudra-kakatiya|Prataparudra]], fled north after the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] took [[e:warangal|Warangal]] in 1323 and established a kingdom among the [[e:gond-people|Gond]] and other peoples of the Bastar plateau. The family goddess [[e:danteshwari|Danteshwari]], enshrined at [[e:dantewada|Dantewada]], became the patron deity of the state.
bastar-state.r: Bastar was thinly populated, densely forested and overwhelmingly Adivasi, with [[e:gond-people|Gond]], Maria, [[e:muria|Muria]] and [[e:halba|Halba]] communities. The Rajas ruled through local headmen and ritual ties, celebrated in the long [[e:bastar-dussehra|Bastar Dussehra]]. In the 18th century the state became tributary to the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]], passing under British control in 1853. The [[e:bhumkal-rebellion|Bhumkal rebellion]] of 1910 against forest restrictions was suppressed by British troops.
bastar-state.e: Bastar merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces]], later [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]], in 1948. Its former ruler [[e:pravir-chandra-bhanj-deo|Pravir Chandra Bhanj Deo]] was killed by police at his palace in 1966. Bastar is now a region of [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

busoga-principalities.t: A cluster of small Basoga principalities east of the Nile, united under the British as a kingdom with an elected ruler, the Kyabazinga.
busoga-principalities.o: From about the 16th century the land between the [[e:nile|Nile]], [[e:lake-victoria|Lake Victoria]] and [[e:lake-kyoga|Lake Kyoga]] was divided among numerous small principalities, many of whose ruling families traced their origins to [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]] and its legendary hunter Mukama. No central kingdom emerged, and the principalities often paid tribute to the more powerful [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Kingdom of Buganda]].
busoga-principalities.r: Each principality was ruled by a hereditary chief with clan heads and village leaders. The economy rested on plantains, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and fishing on the lakes. Under the [[s:uganda-protectorate|Uganda Protectorate]] the British placed Busoga under the [[e:baganda|Ganda]] general [[e:semei-kakungulu|Semei Kakungulu]] in 1906, then created a council of chiefs and, in 1919, the office of [[e:kyabazinga|Kyabazinga]], chosen among the senior chiefs, to head Busoga as a single unit from Bugembe near [[e:jinja|Jinja]].
busoga-principalities.e: The [[e:kyabazinga|Kyabazinga's]] office was abolished with the other Ugandan monarchies in 1967 and restored as a cultural institution in 1995. Kyabazinga [[e:william-wilberforce-nadiope|William Wilberforce Nadiope]] served as Uganda's vice-president in the 1960s.
busoga-principalities.re: Traditional religion, later Christianity and Islam

baoni-state.t: A small Muslim-ruled state in Bundelkhand founded for the former Mughal vizier Imad-ul-Mulk, named after its 52 villages.
baoni-state.o: [[e:ghazi-ud-din-khan-imad-ul-mulk|Ghazi-ud-din Khan Imad-ul-Mulk]], the Mughal [[e:vizier|vizier]] who had deposed [[e:ahmad-shah-bahadur|Ahmad Shah Bahadur]] and murdered [[e:alamgir-ii|Alamgir II]], later took refuge with the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]]. Around 1784 the [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] granted him 52 villages (baoni) in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]], which became the state of Baoni with its seat at Kadaura.
baoni-state.r: Baoni was an 11-gun salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]] ruled by a Nawab over a mostly [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] farming population. Little else of its internal history is recorded.
baoni-state.e: After independence Baoni joined [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] in 1948, and its lands were later transferred to [[e:jalaun-district|Jalaun district]] of [[e:uttar-pradesh|Uttar Pradesh]].
